ECLTeam/EuoraCraft-Launcher.description: EuoraCraft Launcher is a powerful modern Minecraft launcher
ECLTeam/EuoraCraft-Launcher.body:
**A modern third-party Minecraft launcher written in Python, with plugin extensibility. Build your own launcher!**

*Modern Minecraft third-party launcher written in Python, with plugin extensibility, build your own launcher.*

> **Disclaimer**: This launcher is an independent third-party community tool. It has no affiliation, endorsement, or official relationship with Mojang Studios, Microsoft, or any of their subsidiaries.

---

## Introduction

**EuoraCraft Launcher** is a third-party Minecraft launcher that helps you install and start the game, manage different versions and modpacks, and play with friends online. If you are new to Minecraft, you can start with the Quick Start section below.

---

## Features

- **Manage games**: View and launch different versions of the game and modpacks in one place.
- **Add accounts**: Supports Microsoft accounts, offline accounts, and third-party login services.
- **Install modpacks and mods**: Find and install modpacks online, and manage game mods (Mod) and other resources.
- **Multiplayer**: Play with friends.
- **Plugin extensions**: Add plugins as needed to extend launcher functionality.
- **Crash analysis**: When the game errors, helps find possible causes.

---

## Quick Start

1. Open the [download page](https://github.com/ECLTeam/EuoraCraft-Launcher/releases) and choose the version for your operating system (**Windows / Linux / macOS**).
2. Install and open EuoraCraft Launcher, then add an account by following the on-screen prompts.
3. Install the game version or modpack you want to play, then launch the game once it is ready.

> For first-time setup, common questions, and detailed explanations of each feature, see the [documentation site](https://docs.euora.cn).

## Problems or suggestions?

You can first check the [usage documentation and FAQ](https://docs.euora.cn), or [report a problem or make a suggestion](https://github.com/ECLTeam/EuoraCraft-Launcher/issues/new/choose). When reporting, explain what happened and what you did beforehand, and attach screenshots if needed. Remember to hide passwords and other personal information before submitting.

---

行旅录(TransitU) is an Android app focused on reading transit cards and recording trips. Hold your phone near a transit card to read the balance, transaction history, and city route information, and generate statistical charts and trip maps locally.

Jackie2049/perpetual-learning.body:
# perpetual-learning

## Project Overview

A self-evolving intelligent engine that continuously learns, practices, and produces. It learns technical knowledge without interruption, accumulates hands-on experience, discovers directions worth exploring, and produces valuable results. The domain is AI technology, with priority on Infra. When driven by a user, it prioritizes taking on and refining the user's needs and ideas. In real operation, it continuously accumulates reusable hands-on experience. The tasks of tech mining (技术掘金), technical secretary, and experience consolidation are combined organically to keep strengthening the engine's capabilities, ultimately supporting the user's technical outlook, idea exploration, hands-on experience, and industry influence, and making valuable contributions.

[Open the Exploration Workbench ↗](https://jackie2049.github.io/perpetual-learning/) · Browse curated results, search knowledge, review logs and pending decisions.

## How It Works

- **Tech Mining (技术掘金)**: Continuously and autonomously learn, practice, and explore AI technology, prioritizing Infra. Find directions worth pursuing and contributing to, and produce notes, tools, open-source contributions, in-house results, or papers.
- **Technical Secretary (技术秘书)**: Prioritize taking on the user's requirements and vague ideas. Advance goals through due diligence, surveys, value and risk analysis, proofs of concept, and hands-on execution.
- **Experience Consolidation (经验沉淀)**: Accumulate reusable experience from real runs and their feedback, gradually turning it into knowledge, tools, and skills that strengthen future work.

Each piece of work ends with a [log entry](https://github.com/Jackie2049/perpetual-learning/blob/HEAD/diary/readme.md) that preserves results, failures, and changes in judgment, so they can be reviewed and reused. Runtime status and current work are in [WORK.md](https://github.com/Jackie2049/perpetual-learning/blob/HEAD/WORK.md).

### Startup and Control

Start Claude Code in the project directory and give a short command:

```bash
claude "开始运行"
```

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| 开始运行 (Start running) | Automatically read the rules and context, prioritize user tasks, otherwise begin autonomous AI Infra exploration |
| 继续运行 (Continue running) | Resume the previous task and progress |
| 暂停运行 (Pause running) | Save results and next steps, and pause autonomous exploration |
| 查看进展 (Check progress) | Report results, blockers, and next steps |

You can also specify a direction, for example "开始运行，关注推理优化" ("Start running, focus on inference optimization"). Work continues within the current session. After the session ends, restart Claude Code and enter "继续运行" ("Continue running") to resume.

## File Organization

This is the unified entry point for the whole project. Click a path to browse its files, or click the overview to see the content navigation and usage notes for that section.

| Path | Purpose | Overview and Index |

| [README.md](https://github.com/Jackie2049/perpetual-learning/blob/HEAD/README.md) | Project overview, public presentation, and full navigation | This page |

## Introduction

Ever "unconsciously" opened an entertainment app when you wanted to focus? Once you're in and see a full homepage, you forget what you were supposed to be doing?

**FocusCat** can help you:

- **Freely choose apps to restrict**: specify the entertainment or distracting apps you want to control
- **Reflect before entering**: preset reflection questions, and pause to think before entering entertainment pages
- **Positive cat rewards**: each time you finish a reflection and exit an entertainment app, you earn cat food for your cat, raising its affection
- **Timed second reminder**: it's fine if you choose to enter; at a fixed time, your cat will remind you once more
- **Lock-screen focus mode**: screen switching is blocked during full focus, and you earn extra rewards for every half hour of focus

Turn "resisting distraction" from a painful restriction into gentle companionship.

---

| Feature | Description |
|------|------|
| App interception | Shows a reflection Q&A page before opening a restricted app |
| Custom questions | 3 open-ended reflection questions, editable in settings |

| Focus lock | Screen switching is blocked during focus periods; rewards on completing periods |

## iOS App Maintenance

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

If you've modified the blog content, you need to rebuild and sync first:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 16.19.1
MOBILE=1 npm run docs:build

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22.22.2

npx cap open ios
```

Saekisui/hidden-letters-map.description: Treasure Map: hide letters, voice messages, and achievements in real places, so they can only be retrieved when the recipient walks nearby.
Saekisui/hidden-letters-map.body:
# Treasure Map · hidden-letters-map

Hide a letter, a voice message, or an achievement in a real place. On the recipient's map, they only see a blurry circle and a riddle. The item can only be retrieved once they walk nearby.

- **Treasure hider**: hides things at a place, draws travel routes, and publishes achievements directly. Operates through an MCP client such as Claude Code / Claude Desktop, or directly via curl.
- **Treasure seeker**: opens a web page on their phone (added to the home screen and used like an app). The map shows the planned route, their own position and footprints, fog circles, and riddles. Walking into a circle lets them open the envelope. Opened items go to the detail page. Earned achievements hang on the achievement wall. They can also pin an “I was here” marker at their current spot and leave a message.

Sealed letters: the data the page receives contains no place names, coordinates, or body text, and it cannot be peeked at in the developer tools either.

---

## Getting it running

Requires Node 20.6 or above.

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env     # At minimum, change PASSWORD, and fill in the two people's names too
npm run build            # Builds the page to dist/
npm start                # Default http://localhost:3000
```

Open it in a browser and enter the password. The treasure seeker's phone must be able to reach this address from outside. Either host it on a machine with a public address, or expose a home machine using something like Cloudflare Tunnel or Tailscale Funnel. **Location reporting and push notifications both require https.**

On iPhone: open in Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen. Only opening from the home screen gives full-screen mode and allows receiving push notifications.

Settings available in `.env`:

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `PASSWORD` | Required. Used for page login, MCP, and location app reporting |
| `PORT` | Default 3000 |
| `DATA_DIR` | Data directory, default `./data` |
| `HIDER_NAME` / `FINDER_NAME` | How the two people are addressed on the page: the letter's signature “—— 阿笙” and the “FOR 小满 · WITH LOVE” ring on achievements |
| `TZ` | Time zone used to count a day for “unlocks after visiting for several days”. If unset, the system time zone is used |
| `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` / `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` / `VAPID_SUBJECT` | For push notifications. Optional, see below |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` | For Street View. Optional, see below |

---

| Tool | Purpose |

Trojankill/Safe-server-lists-for-bypassi.description: Filtering of insecure servers in public subscriptions
Trojankill/Safe-server-lists-for-bypassi.body:
# 🛡️ VPN Config Security Filter

---

## 🚀 What's new in v6.0

The main change: **every link is now actually parsed**, rather than checked with regexes against the raw string. Percent-encoding is decoded, `&` and `\u0026` are repaired, and parameter synonyms are reduced to one name. Everything that previously passed as "unreadable — therefore fine" is now rejected.

### 🔬 Parsing and normalization

- ✅ **URI parser instead of regex** — vless / vmess / trojan / hysteria2 / ss / tuic are parsed into a structure
- ✅ **Double decoding** — `&amp;`, `\u0026`, `%5Cu0026`, `¬`
- ✅ **Invisible characters** — zero-width, BOM, `\n`, control chars are stripped before checking
- ✅ **Parameter synonyms** — `allowlnsecure` (with a lowercase L), `skip-cert-verify`, `skip_cert_verify`, `insecure`
- ✅ **Lowercase scheme** — `VLESS://` no longer breaks parsing
- ✅ **Insecurity flags** — any value other than an explicit `0/false/no/off` is treated as enabled
- ✅ **vmess `"tls":"none"`** — no longer passes as valid TLS
- ✅ **Duplicates before limits** — one node with different names no longer crowds out legitimate configs

### 🌐 Addresses and protocols

- ✅ **`ipaddress` instead of regex** — 169.254/16, 100.64/10, 198.18/15,…

Yang-Code01/jlpt-library.body:
# Personal Workbench

An offline-capable personal workbench with two learning tracks, Japanese (JLPT N1–N5) and English (word frequency 1k–4k), plus AI research reports and documentation and downloads for self-built tools. The home page is organized into three sections: **Language Learning**, **Research Reports**, and **Tool Development**. There is no build step and no external dependencies; it works by opening `file://` directly.

🌐 **Online browsing**: https://Yang-Code01.github.io/jlpt-library/

## Modules

The portal `index.html` is the unified entry point for all modules, built as a workbench shell: a **180px persistent navigation sidebar on the left** (4 sections, plus 11 modules within the Language Learning section, which can be collapsed) + a **48px top bar** (section name / module type filter / search box) + **single-column cards**.
The right column of each card shows learning progress (`Viewed 12 / 168`). The denominator comes from `assets/units.js`, generated by `tools/portal.mjs`, and the numerator comes from browser-local progress. Japanese and English appear as two sub-group headings within the Language Learning section, and **there is no longer a language toggle** (see `docs/adr/0010`).

| Module | Entry | Content |
|---|---|---|
| **Study Materials** | `material/index.html` | Basic knowledge, grammar, and vocabulary from N5 → N1, 168 unit pages in total; Japanese content includes furigana readings, and each unit includes a self-test |
| **Past Paper Practice** | `exam/index.html` | Question-type drills (by subtype / by past-paper order) and full mock exams (155 minutes, listening section last, audio plays only once); the N2 July 2023 and December 2023 papers are already included |
| **Classroom Vocabulary** | `jp-vocab/index.html` | Flashcards grouped by classroom topic (adverbs, idiomatic expressions, word formation, etc.), 11 units / 633 cards in total; four modes: browse, flip cards, quiz, and spaced-repetition review. Words and example sentences have audio (the unit 「単語の前に漢字をプラス」 has no audio yet). 「様子の副詞」 also has a focused 15-word mode |
| **English Vocabulary** | `en/1k/01.html` onward | Divided into four tiers by word frequency: 1k / 2k / 3k / 4k, with 50 words per unit. The list and flip-card modes are available for memorization; quizzes and spaced-repetition review are being added to each unit page gradually. Data is generated from ECDICT by `tools/en-vocab.mjs` |
| **English Dictation** | `en/dictation/index.html` | 77 word lists, one-to-one with the vocabulary units. Listen to English pronunciation and spell the word (uses the browser's built-in speech, no pre-generated audio). Playback count, Chinese gloss, and word order are adjustable; a wrong-word notebook allows focused review; and "words already practiced no longer appear" can be turned off. The core engine is shared with Japanese dictation via a single `dictation/dictation.js` |

# IOTA Watch

An open-source, five-language, multi-project monitoring dashboard centered on **IOTA Train at Home**. It supports IOTA, XID / MMM, Quantus, fly.ai, Nosana, Gonka, Akash, io.net, Vast.ai and Golem; each project's inputs, cycles, and data coverage are described separately.

IOTA Train at Home (Macrocosmos / Bittensor SN9) is the core project, with ten project pages covering training, mining and compute. Tool pages query records; separate tutorials explain identifiers, fields and troubleshooting. Public projects use public identifiers; io.net and Vast.ai require account connections with read credentials. Those two integrations have mocked validation; real-account validation remains pending.

- **Training history**: view training tokens, throughput, and cumulative tokens by day, week, or month; missing data is left as gaps.

# lean-electron-vue

A ready-to-use desktop app development template for **Vite + Electron + Vue 3 + TypeScript**

Simplified Chinese | [English](https://github.com/mrcen3204097569-spec/lean-electron-vue/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

## Introduction

An Electron template that does not depend on third-party integration solutions such as `electron-vite` or `vite-plugin-electron`. Two very thin custom Vite plugins connect Vite and Electron. The entire build process is only a few dozen lines of code, **easy to understand and easy to modify**.

- `pnpm dev`: starts the Vite dev server, compiles the main process with esbuild, then automatically launches Electron. The dev server URL is passed in via the environment variable `VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL`. The renderer process supports HMR
- `pnpm build`: builds the renderer process and compiles the main process, producing a runnable `dist/` without calling electron-builder
- `pnpm dist`: on top of `pnpm build`, calls electron-builder to generate an installer package
- `pnpm test`: runs pure-logic unit tests with Vitest (`app://` path validation, update notes YAML, window policy, CSP)

- ⚡️ **Vite 8 + Vue 3.5 + TypeScript**, `<script setup>` syntax, second-level ultra-fast hot reload
- 🧩 **Native plugin architecture (Plugin Engine)**: supports plugin lifecycle (`setup` / `teardown`), isolated storage space, dynamic route injection, status bar widget mounting, command registration, and dedicated configuration panels
- 🌐 **Community plugin marketplace (Marketplace)**: an Obsidian / VS Code-style plugin store that supports seamless dynamic hot loading and one-click install and uninstall. Built-in curated extensions include a Pomodoro focus timer, a clipboard history guard, a design color palette, and a REST API debugger
- 🔍 **Raycast-style global command palette (`Ctrl+K` / `Cmd+K`)**: millisecond fuzzy search, instant navigation to any app page, triggering of system-level shortcut functions, and dynamic aggregation of plugin custom commands

## Table of Contents

- [Project Overview](#-项目简介)

---

### 💡 Project Overview

**医不帮 (yibubang)** is an open-source, cross-platform professional question-practice tool for medical students. Traditional quiz apps often suffer from pain points such as mandatory online connectivity, bloated ads, lack of desktop support, and question banks tied to a single app. 医不帮 uses **Flutter** and an **Offline-First** approach to deliver a consistent, smooth, high-performance practice experience on phones, tablets, and computers (Android, Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS).

The project uses a fully decoupled architecture of "**physically split multiple question banks + globally shared user state**." Question banks and answer data are physically isolated. This allows hundreds of thousands of professional medical questions to be practiced on demand, while users' answer records, wrong answers, favorites, and practice history remain safely stored locally.

---

### ✨ Core Features

- 💻 **Seamless cross-platform desktop and mobile use**
  - Native support for Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux; iOS/iPadOS support in progress.
  - Supports keyboard shortcuts for page turning, responsive large-screen desktop layouts, and one-handed mobile optimization.
- ⚡️ **Second-level fast cold start, clean and ad-free**
  - No launch ads, no forced privacy collection, no bundled promotions; reaches the practice screen in milliseconds.
  - Uses file-fingerprint cache validation, so cold-starting a SQLite database of hundreds of megabytes takes less than 5 milliseconds.
- 🎯 **Diverse practice and review modes**
  - **Practice mode**: Instant right/wrong feedback, with detailed explanations, exam year attribution, knowledge-point tags, and high-resolution images.
  - **Quick mode**: Focused, efficient practice with automatic progression to increase question throughput.
  - **Test mode**: Simulates an exam environment with hidden answers and instant feedback, a bottom status bar for quick submission, and a full-dimension quiz report.
  - **Recitation mode**: Displays reference answers and detailed explanations directly, a useful tool for last-minute exam memorization.
  - **Multi-dimensional filters**: Flexibly filter by question type (single/multiple choice), mastery status (all/mastered/not mastered), and answer category (all/wrong/favorited/unattempted).
- 📊 **Learning statistics dashboard and visual heatmap**
  - Millisecond-level answer time tracking (`duration`) that precisely records how long each question takes.
  - A GitHub-style "**question grid wall / activity heatmap**" that visually shows daily question volume and focused review time.

PintreeNewTab is an open-source project based on [Pintree](https://github.com/Pintree-io/pintree), designed to turn browser bookmarks into a tab page. By installing the extension, bookmarks that are inconvenient to manage are converted into a beautiful and easy-to-use navigation page.

- Traditional Chinese

1. Install the Edge ([PintreeNewTab](https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/pintreenewtab/mjiogedjmkbihhahaljlefekjbcgplog)) and Chrome ([PintreeNewTab](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/ekfkalhnkifkoijcioheanlegfgcgnee)) extensions.

vibevalleyhq/vibevalley.description: Coder Farm Tales · A team of coding agents you direct by voice or chat, drawn as a pixel farm. Runs on your own machine.
vibevalleyhq/vibevalley.body:
> A team of coding agents you direct by voice or chat, drawn as a pixel farm. Runs on your own machine.

**VibeValley** (码农场物语) is a team of coding agents you command by voice or typing, drawn as a pixel farm.

You only talk to the **butler** (管家). The butler assigns jobs to **hands** (帮工), which are real coding agents on your machine (pi, Claude Code, Codex……). They open branches in your project, change code, run tests, and commit. The crops in the field grow according to their real progress: they sprout when code is read, grow leaves when files are changed, and yield wheat when the work is done. You review the **harvest list** (收成清单) before merging a branch into the main branch.

You, the butler, and the hands talk in the same group chat, the **field edge** (田头): each job has a ticket thread attached below it, where the hands confirm, ask questions, and report, and you can jump in anytime. In short, VibeValley is an AI version of Linear that runs on your machine: tickets are assigned to coding agents that work in the project turn by turn, and you review the changes before merging. The farm is the skin on the outside ([concepts](https://github.com/vibevalleyhq/vibevalley/blob/HEAD/docs/concepts.md)).

> [!WARNING]
> The hands have **no permission prompts and no sandbox**, and can run arbitrary commands on this machine. The server listens only on `127.0.0.1`; do not expose it to the network. Only put projects you are willing to hand over to coding agents into the working directory.

## What it can do

- **Assigning and harvesting work**: tell the butler "add an endpoint in clock-in that queries clock-in records, and write tests." The butler picks a suitable hand and either gives it its own branch and worktree, per the profile settings, or has it work in the project directory. When it's done, you check the commits, the diff, and whether there are conflicts, then merge into the main branch once confirmed. If there are conflicts, have the hand resolve them itself.
- **Several jobs at once**: up to 6 hands can work in the field at the same time; hands using worktrees each have independent branches.
- **Map**: each project is a small island. The plots on the island correspond to the tickets being worked on and the open slots that can still take assignments. Queued jobs are seed bags outside the courtyard gate; click an open slot to write a ticket for that project.
- **See the process**: every step of each hand is recorded as a trajectory, including the messages it receives, each command and its output, and what it says. If a step goes wrong, you can comment on that specific step and it will keep revising.
- **Planting plans**: for long tasks, first have a hand read the code and break it into an ordered step diagram; you review the draft before work starts. Steps that don't depend on each other are done in parallel, and each step is merged into the plan branch only after it passes checks; finally, the plan is brought into the main branch in one go. When fixing a bug, the first step writes a **failing acceptance test**; later steps may not change it, and the final step must make it pass.
- **Channels, schedules, and patrols**: open channels per project; scheduled tasks such as "run the tests every day at nine"; and model-free patrols that remind you of questions no one has answered, hands with no activity, and finished jobs that haven't been collected.
-…
